## Open

### F-001 — Rewriting a whole file is only safe when fences are tracked

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

The first version of the blank-line handling collapsed runs inside fenced code blocks, which
silently changes a sample that contains a blank line. The wrapper now tracks fences, and leaves
tables, headings, the meta line and HTML comments alone. Lesson: a formatter that rewrites a file
has to model the syntax it must preserve, not only the syntax it changes.

### F-002 — A move between two root areas deleted the entry

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

move read the target file, inserted the entry, then removed it from the source read taken earlier.
When both areas live in the same file (cross-cutting to ci) those were the same document: the entry
was written twice and then removed once, so it vanished. Found by smoke testing the verbs in a
scratch workspace rather than by the unit tests, which each covered one operation in isolation. The
fix edits the meta line in place when the target is the same file.

### F-003 — A second write to the same file overwrote the first batch

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

migrate grouped work by area, but every root area (cross-cutting, ci, docs) lives in the same root
document: the second area rebuilt the document from the skeleton and wrote it over the first batch,
silently dropping 18 entries. Group by target file, keep one document per file, write once.

### F-004 — A stale line range spliced items into the index block

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

ensureManualSection returned the section parsed before refreshIndex moved the file, so
addManualItems spliced the 32 migrated manual items inside the index block; the next refresh
replaced that range and the items were gone, with no error. Re-read the structure after the refresh:
any line range from parseDoc is invalidated by a refresh.

### F-130 — `tap`'s positional globs bypass its own `exclude` rules

> _2026-09-12 · tools/blong-dev · open_

`blong-dev test` passes `'*.test.ts' '**/*.test.ts'` as positional test files, and tap then ignores
both its default excludes (folders named `dist`, `fixture`, `fixtures`) and an explicit
`--exclude=…`, so a package's generated fixture directory runs as part of the package suite.

Four things were tried before accepting that: `--exclude` after the globs, `--exclude` before them,
a negated glob (`'!test/fixture/**'`), and dropping the globs entirely. Dropping them works, but
tap's default `include` then also picks up Playwright specs and layer files that merely live under
`test/`.

Fixing it properly means `blong-dev test` honoring a package-level tap config instead of hard-coding
globs — a shared-tool change with repo-wide blast radius.

### F-081 — The blong-dev package has no ci-test script and no eslint config

> _2026-09-12 · tools/blong-dev · open_

`tools/blong-dev` has no `ci-test` script, so `npm run ci-test` there errors, and it has no eslint
config either, so `blong-dev lint` prints two check marks instead of three. Both are normal for this
package: neither is a failure, and neither should be "fixed" as part of an unrelated change.

### F-201 — A comma in a memory title is silently rejected

> _2026-09-19 · tools/blong-dev · open_

blong-dev memory add decision --title with a comma in it prints the command usage instead of an
error naming the bad value, so the entry is simply not written and nothing says why. Cost two
attempts here; the body may contain commas, the title may not. A title with a comma should either be
taken literally or refused with a message that names it.

### F-217 — memory add rejects a colon in the title, and says nothing useful about it

> _2026-09-21 · tools/blong-dev · open_

A title containing a colon - "A condition that had always been an object: fixing it..." - makes
`blong-dev memory add` print the whole memory usage block instead of an error, so the entry is
simply not written and the reason is not stated. It cost two attempts to spot, because the same body
text with a colon-free title is accepted and the `add` verb takes no `--body-file`, so the first fix
attempt was invalid for a second reason. Worth either quoting the offending argument or rejecting it
by name.

### F-263 — tap cannot write its raw stream to /dev/stdout through a pipe

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Telling tap to write its raw TAP stream to `/dev/stdout` and relaying that stream works only when
the stdout of the process that spawned tap is a regular file. As the child of a Node process it is a
pipe, and tap opens the output path for truncation, which fails with a no-such-device error. The
same invocation succeeds from a shell with a redirect, which is what makes the trap easy to walk
into: the experiment passes and the code does not.

What works instead is the follower now in the runner: tap writes the stream to `tap.raw.tap` and
`blong-dev` reads whatever is new from that file on a short interval, echoing it in a watched run
and stopping when the run does. Nothing is buffered, a file that does not exist yet is not an error,
and a tap that buffers its own output is simply echoed at the end.

### F-266 — A tap run has one reporter, which cost four attempts to work around

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Wanting both a live run and a machine report from one `tap` invocation cost several attempts, and
each one failed for a different reason worth remembering.

`TAP=1` does give the raw TAP on stdout while a reporter is configured, but it also overrides the
reporter: the json file is never written, so it cannot be combined with `--reporter-file`.

`--output-file` makes tap echo the child's stream twice on stdout, once as the reporter renders it
and once as the raw TAP it writes, so a watched run cannot keep that artifact that way.

`tap replay` does render a stream back into a report, and it reads that stream on stdin, which makes
it the one way to have both — but only if the stream handed to it is the run that just happened.
Replaying what tap recorded instead replayed whatever recording was newest, which included entries
whose files were already gone and turned a green run red with an error about a missing `.tap` file.

The shape that survived is the simple one: a run is either watched or captured, and the report
belongs to the captured run.

### F-267 — Two Allure producers cannot share one results directory

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · open_

An Allure session clears the results directory it writes to, which is fine for one producer and
quietly wrong for two. Pointing the handler-test runner at the directory the browser reporter
already uses would have made the published report depend on which of them ran last:
`realm/blong-access` runs `blong-dev test` and then `blong-dev playwright` in one test script, so
the browser results would have won every time and the handler tests would have vanished from the
report without an error.

Worth remembering for the next producer: the name of that directory is now the only thing separating
two reports, and it belongs in `ALLURE_RESULTS_DIRS` beside the merge.

### F-273 — Joining a report failure to the history by name

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Attributing each failing test to the base branch needed a join between two files that share no key:
the report entry has a name and the history record has a fullName, Allure's result id turned out to
change between runs of the same test, and the two producers do not share a separator (the browser
leg writes file › suite › title, the handler leg realm.collection.group.step). The effort went into
discovering all of that by hand, and the lesson is to measure the data before designing the key: two
throw-away scripts over .github/history.jsonl showed that only 10 of 302 tests are unreachable by
bare name and that id is useless as an identity, which turned a speculative plan to plumb historyId
through every runner into the small normalisation that shipped. The second lesson is that the
harness fixture is the only place the rendered report is asserted, so a new stat cannot be asserted
until the fixture carries data for it — the fixture is written first, and its expectations are
copied from a real report:local run rather than guessed.

### F-280 — CI=1 locally stops at a sudo prompt from playwright install --with-deps

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Running the suite with `CI=1` locally makes `blong-dev playwright` run
`playwright install --with-deps`, which shells out to the system package manager and stops the run
at a `[sudo] password` prompt that nothing in an agent session can answer. The flag that disables it
already exists — `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_INSTALL=1`, which the CI workflow sets for the same reason
(parallel package-manager lock contention) — so a local run that has to look like CI should start as
`CI=1 PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_INSTALL=1 <command>`. Cost: two runs of `blong-dev test` in a package whose
e2e leg runs a fixture's playwright command, both abandoned at the prompt before any evidence was
collected, plus a detour looking for the sudo in the package's own scripts, where it does not
appear.

### F-314 — A timed-out suite leaves its dev server holding the port

> _2026-09-29 · tools/blong-dev · open_

When a Playwright or tap run is cut off by a timeout, the dev server it started keeps listening: the
next run that needs the same port fails with an address-already-in-use error, and in this session
that showed up as three failures in core/blong-gogo's graceful-shutdown spawn test rather than as a
port problem — the spawned CLI could not bind 8080 because a blong dev server from an earlier
aborted run still had it. Check the port before reading a spawn-test failure as a code failure, and
prefer a suite that owns its ports over one that competes for the defaults.

### F-317 — The format pass re-wrapped the user's own Manual list

> _2026-09-29 · tools/blong-dev · open_

The format pass re-wrapped the user's own ## Manual list in the root todo.md into one run-on
paragraph. The checker exempts that section, because it is the user's and not the tool's, but the
formatter re-rendered the whole document and knew nothing about sections - so the one command
documented as safe to run anywhere tidied the one thing the house rules say agents never touch, and
the damage is silent (it reads as prose and passes check). formatLines now treats ## Manual as
verbatim to the next heading, with a test. The lesson is wider than this section: a re-render must
carry every exemption the checker applies, or the gate and the writer disagree about what is owned -
the same shape as the T-175 rules, where the wrapper produced what the checker rejected.

### F-324 — Node type stripping rejects TS parameter properties

> _2026-09-30 · tools/blong-dev · open_

`constructor(readonly url: string)` type-checks under `tsc --noEmit` and runs under tap, which
compiles with swc, but the CLI died with `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX` the first time the new
module was loaded: Node runs these sources in strip-only mode, where a parameter property is
unsupported syntax rather than something it can erase. Declare the fields and assign them in the
constructor body instead — and run the binary once after adding a module, because a green test suite
does not prove the module loads.

### F-325 — A cached stats read made a finished ingest look stuck

> _2026-09-30 · tools/blong-dev · open_

`GET /v1/default/banks/{bank}/stats` is cached for 60 seconds, and it reported
`pending_operations: 2` with `total_documents: 0` for half a minute after the worker log had already
printed STREAMING RETAIN COMPLETE — so a working ingest read as a hang, and the first instinct was
to debug the CLI. Add `?refresh=true` before concluding an operation is stuck, and check the
operations list, which is not cached. The same trap applies to the rendered output: the similarity
the CLI prints comes from `scores.semantic`, because `scores.final` is not comparable between
queries and a clearly relevant match ranks first at `0.0006`.

### F-326 — A bank can hold a fraction of the tree and still read as healthy

> _2026-09-30 · tools/blong-dev · open_

While building the embedding benchmark the bank reported 54 documents, 0 pending and 0 failed
operations — a state that reads as a working index. The tree holds 591 entries, and only 4 of the
benchmark's 36 targets were in it. Nothing compares the two: `blong-dev memory index --semantic`
reports on what it sent ("591 of 591 entries ingested"), never on what the bank holds, and
`memory search` answers out of whatever is there. The first benchmark pass was therefore a read of a
partial corpus that looked like a complete one, and only an intersection against
`memory list --json` exposed it. Printing the bank's own document count next to the backfill's total
would have made the gap visible in the first line of output.

### F-336 — A markdownlint rule id with three segments was read as no diagnostic

> _2026-10-01 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Probing the T-187 fix with a file whose first line was prose printed a green tick and exited 1:
parseMarkdownlint matched MD\d+/[\w-]+, which expects exactly two segments, while markdownlint
reports MD041/first-line-heading/first-line-h1. The diagnostic was dropped while the tool's exit
code still failed the run, which is the worst combination — a pass that is not one, and one that had
been hiding real findings for as long as the tool has emitted multi-segment ids. Lesson: when a
parser reads a third-party tool's output, feed it a line the tool actually printed rather than a
hand-written one, and treat a non-zero exit with no parsed diagnostics as a parser bug.

### F-337 — The bank listing lagged the queued backfill

> _2026-10-01 · tools/blong-dev · open_

The first live index --semantic --sources docs,skill --stats reported "bank holds 0 document(s) of
this source, tree holds 128" immediately after ingesting 128, because the write hook queues
ingestion (async: true) and the listing ran before the server had stored anything. The repair path
now waits, through retain(..., {wait: true}), which is what makes the coverage line a fact rather
than a guess. A second defect fell out of the same probe: the listing loop advanced by the page size
it asked for rather than the size it received, so a server that caps a page below the limit would be
asked for offsets it can never reach. Lesson: a check that reads a store right after writing it has
to know whether the write was queued, and a paging loop must advance by what came back.

### F-383 — memory show --json gives the body as lines, and printing them writes a list

> _2026-10-05 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Piping the JSON body of an entry into python3 -c print writes a Python list literal into the
markdown file, and the damage is quiet: memory check reports zero errors, because the shape it
validates is a wrapped paragraph with a stray quote in it, while the package's own lint fails on the
line with markdown/no-missing-label-refs pointing at a label that is the whole body. Use the CLI's
own flags for a body (a heredoc into memory edit --body-file), never a round trip through the JSON,
and lint the package whose memory file was touched rather than the repository root alone.

### F-386 — docs check needs a broker and fails without one

> _2026-10-06 · tools/blong-dev · open_

blong-dev docs check runs each generated artefact's generator, and realm.observed-flows failed with
broker transport failure (code -195) because the log/broker server is not running, so the check
exits non-zero before it reaches a verdict on anything else. Nothing in the message names the
missing dependency, so the failure reads like a documentation problem: say which service the
generator needs, and do not treat a failure on that artefact as a docs regression.

### F-401 — A todo's premise can be stale; the code is the premise

> _2026-10-06 · tools/blong-dev · open_

T-230 was written when the id counter ran per memory file, so a bare id could name two entries. By
the time it was implemented, highestId already scans every file and nextId allocates one number
across the workspace, so the collision the todo described no longer happens from ordinary adds. The
first version of the fixtures was written to the todo rather than to the code - two adds in two
packages, expecting two T-001s - and the tests failed, not because the resolution was wrong but
because the setup produced T-001 and T-002. A duplicate now only arrives from a pinned --id, a batch
import, or a migration, and the fixtures had to build that state explicitly. Lesson: read the
allocation code before writing a fixture that assumes a collision, and check a todo's premise
against the source before implementing it.

### F-408 — glossary export collides with memory removeEntry

> _2026-10-07 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Re-exporting the new glossary module with `export * from ./glossary/glossaryDoc.ts` in
`tools/blong-dev/src/index.ts` failed tsc with TS2308: `removeEntry` is already exported by
`memory/memoryEdit.ts`. Renamed the glossary functions to `addTerm`, `removeTerm`, `findTerm`,
`renderTerm` and `sortTerms` (clearer anyway, the glossary unit is a term) with the rename-symbol
tool, which updated the command and both test files. Lesson: with many `export *` from one index,
check the exported names of a new module against the existing ones before wiring it in, and give
domain functions a domain word to avoid the collision.

### F-442 — A closed todo's id is handed to the next entry

> _2026-10-08 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Migrating an item with `blong-dev memory close` removes it unless `--keep` is given, and the next
`memory add` takes the id it freed: closing the item about the CR carrying a service switch let the
item about the operator never deleting obsolete objects take T-279, so every comment that cited the
closed work — in the realm's generator, plan and tests, and in an e2e script — silently changed
meaning to point at a different, still open, unrelated defect. Nothing warns: `memory audit` reports
dangling references and duplicate ids, and this is neither, because the reference resolves. Lesson:
cite an entry that will still exist, and close with `--keep` when the id is cited anywhere in code —
the id is a name in prose, and prose is what a reader trusts.

## Resolved

### F-080 — `blong-dev` CLI not built

> _2026-09-11 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

— `npm run ci-lint` (`blong-dev lint`) fails with
`Cannot find module .../blong-dev/bin/blong-dev.ts`, so eslint/cspell could not be run from the
package. Fell back to the VS Code `get_errors` diagnostics (clean) + file-local cspell disables.
Needs a `rush build` of `tools/blong-dev` to run the real lint locally.

### F-090 — `blong-dev` was not built, so `npm run ci-lint` could not find it

> _2026-09-12 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

`npm run ci-lint` (`blong-dev lint`) failed with
`Cannot find module .../blong-dev/bin/blong-dev.ts`, so eslint and cspell could not be run from the
package. The fallback was the VS Code `get_errors` diagnostics (clean) plus file-local
`/* spell-checker: disable */` comments, which is the repo's documented convention for theme files.

Running the real lint locally needs a `rush build` of `tools/blong-dev` first.

### F-103 — `blong-dev sql` went unused because the dev DB name was unknown

> _2026-08-19 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

`blong-dev sql` now derives the dev DB name (`${suite}-${user}`, e.g. `blong-access-kalin`) when
none is configured — from the `.blong_devrc` `suite` key, else the `package.json` name in the cwd,
else `--suite`; the user comes from the OS user — and renders `${suite}`/`${user}` templates. It is
documented as the intended way to query the DB in the blong-schema and blong-adapter skills and in
`copilot-instructions.md`, to be used instead of a MySQL CLI or `kubectl exec`.

### F-104 — `blong-dev sql` connected as an anonymous user

> _2026-08-21 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

`readConnection` started from `{}` and only layered `.blong_devrc`/CLI values, so with no `srv.db`
in `.blong_devrc` the connection had no user or password and MySQL answered
`Access denied for user ''@'...'`. The fix falls back to the shared `srv.db` adapter's dev defaults
(`blong-admin`/`password` at `localhost:3306`) for the default `srv.db` key only — custom `--config`
keys stay empty — and auto-creates the derived dev database (`${suite}-${user}`) when it is missing,
mirroring the dev intent's `createDatabase: true`. A dev tool should mirror the framework's own dev
connection defaults instead of requiring per-developer `.blong_devrc` setup.

### F-327 — lint --files silently checks nothing when given a list

> _2026-09-30 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

`blong-dev lint --files` takes exactly one path. A comma-joined list is read as a single path that
does not exist, so nothing is checked and the command still prints `✓ cspell: 2 file(s)` and
`✓ markdown: 2 file(s)`. Probed with a file holding a deliberate misspelling: alone it reports
`Unknown word`; comma-joined with a clean file it reports success; space-separated it checks the
first path only and prints no second-file summary. Nine changed files passed in one call therefore
produced a green lint that had examined none of them, and the embedding-model comparison document
reached a review pass carrying a missing dictionary word and six misaligned table pipes. Lint one
path per call, believe the file count rather than the tick, and keep `ci-lint` (a whole-package
`tsc --noEmit`) as the check that reports honestly.

the flag is parsed in core/blong-lint and a run now refuses a path that does not exist, an unknown
option and a path no tool reads, so a green tick over nothing is no longer reachable; the guidance
to lint one path per call is withdrawn

### F-385 — A targeted lint of a skill file reports three words that predate it

> _2026-10-05 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

frontmatter, MODELSPEC and FRONTMATTER are unknown to cspell in
.github/skills/_shared/conventions.md, so blong-dev lint --files on that file fails with three
errors that are not caused by the edit while markdownlint and tsc pass. Either the file is excluded
when a package is linted or the three words belong in the dictionary, but a targeted lint there is
misleading for whoever touches the file next.

The three words are in the dictionary now (blong-dev cspell add frontmatter MODELSPEC FRONTMATTER),
so a targeted lint of .github/skills/_shared/conventions.md passes: cspell and markdown both clean.
